subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput recap & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Rivera <ethan.rivera@finpay.com>, Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput recap & next steps

Hi Ethan / Samantha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the options we discussed so we have a shared view before we size next steps: 

Summary of requirements (as discussed)
- Primary use: real-time fraud/transaction scoring for web and mobile flows
- Target latency: p95 <= 60ms (goal is <50ms if possible)
- Peak real-time traffic: ~300 QPS (observed spikes up to ~450 for short bursts)
- Nightly batch: ~200k requests across a ~6 hour window for retraining / backfill
- Data sensitivity: PCI-adjacent, need audit logs and optional VPC connectivity (but currently not air-gapped)

Options we covered
1) Hosted API (Redwood-hosted) — fastest to integrate, simple quotas and scaling. Good if you can tolerate some multi-tenant variability; works well for lower committed QPS and when you want minimal ops overhead.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool in your account/tenant with predictable throughput, configurable autoscaling, and SLA-backed latency/uptime. Best fit for predictable 24/7 traffic and tighter p95 targets.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — recommended when you need customer-managed networking, strict compliance, or full air-gapped deployments. Longer setup and onboarding timeline.

Preliminary recommendation (engineering view to follow): for a sustained peak ~300 QPS with p95 ~60ms we typically recommend Dedicated capacity to meet predictable latency targets while controlling unit cost. Hosted can be a good short pilot if you want to validate model quality quickly; Private doesn't look necessary at this stage unless your compliance team requires it.

Next steps / asks
- Ethan/Samantha: confirm whether the 300 QPS is sustained or if it represents short spikes (and share typical payload size / token count).
- If possible, please share a sample payload and the network diagram (we can use a redacted sample).
- We'll run a short profiling run (Neha) and come back with an estimated Dedicated sizing (+ cost delta) and a recommended pilot path on Hosted so you can validate accuracy.

Attachments: SLA-diff-table.xlsx (high-level SLA and feature differences)

I'll follow up with a sizing note from Neha later today and a one-page mutual action plan for approvals/POs.

Thanks —
Dylan

Thanks Dylan — this is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- The 300 QPS is generally sustained during business hours (9am-6pm ET) with short spikes up to ~450 for a couple of minutes.
- Average payload is ~512 tokens (we use short transaction + context), so per-request token count is modest.
- Nightly batch: confirm 200k across 6 hours (mostly low-priority) — can tolerate higher latency there.

Attaching our network diagram (redacted) for connectivity questions.

Also can you give ballpark pricing for: Hosted pilot (2 weeks, up to 150k tokens/day) vs Dedicated baseline monthly with the above sustained profile? We need to show rough numbers to procurement.

Quick sizing notes after looking at the profile Ethan shared on the call: 
- Given sustained 300 QPS and p95 target ~60ms, Dedicated with reserved GPUs is the safer path for predictable p95. Hosted can be bursty on multi-tenant hardware and may occasionally exceed p95 targets during noisy neighbor events.
- Pilot approach: run a 2-week Hosted pilot to validate model outputs and integration, then migrate to Dedicated for production SLA. We can use the pilot to collect real traffic profiles and tune batching/cache.

Recommended Dedicated baseline (initial estimate)
- GPU type: A10 / A30 class (cost-effective) or A100 if they need the absolute lowest latency; start with A10x6 nodes + autoscale headroom (equivalent ~6 GPUs) for 300 sustained QPS with batching tuned to their 512-token average.
- Expected p95: ~40-70ms depending on GPU choice and sequence length.
- Nightly batch: run on the same pool off-peak or schedule to cheaper instances (no special infra required).

Data we need from FinPay to firm numbers: average tokenized sequence length distribution, exact payload size, concurrency breakdown (web vs async), and expected growth over 6/12 months.

I'll prepare a short perf-run plan (Jenkins job + sample payload) and share a link to the benchmark results once complete. Recommend we include a 2-week Hosted pilot in the MAP and then a 30-day validation phase on Dedicated prior to committing to an annual reserved contract.

-Neha
